entities.name: Cleopatra III of Egypt
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cleopatra III, also known as Cleopatra Euergetis ("Benefactress"), was a formidable Ptolemaic queen who co-ruled Egypt for over four decades between 142 BCE and 101 BCE, navigating a complex web of dynastic struggles, political intrigue, and Roman influence. Her reign was marked by an unprecedented struggle for power within the Ptolemaic royal family, directly impacting the stability and foreign policy of one of the Hellenistic world's most enduring kingdoms. Born into the ruling dynasty, her ambition and political acumen were central to the late Ptolemaic period, as she actively participated in the selection and deposition of her co-rulers and sons, shaping the course of Egyptian governance during a critical era of increasing Roman ascendancy.

Initially, Cleopatra III reigned alongside her mother, Cleopatra II, and her uncle-husband, Ptolemy VIII Physcon, from 142 to 131 BCE. This period was characterized by intense civil war, known as the "Ptolemaic Civil War" or "Brother-Sister War," which saw Alexandria itself divided and ravaged. After Ptolemy VIII's return from Cyprus in 127 BCE, she resumed co-rule with him until his death in 116 BCE. Upon his demise, Ptolemy VIII's will stipulated that Cleopatra III should choose one of her two sons, Ptolemy IX Soter II or Ptolemy X Alexander I, to rule alongside her. Her preference for Ptolemy X, despite popular support for Ptolemy IX, sparked further conflict, leading to Ptolemy IX's exile and recall multiple times, as Cleopatra III continuously maneuvered to maintain her authority, even attempting to assassinate Ptolemy IX in 101 BCE.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Cleopatra III's long and turbulent reign profoundly destabilized the Ptolemaic kingdom through relentless dynastic infighting, paving the way for increased Roman intervention and accelerating the dynasty's eventual decline. Her actions directly contributed to a prolonged civil war and set a precedent for the intense power struggles that characterized the final century of independent Egypt.
